CapabilityProfile.description:
Capability profile artifact for a system under assessment.

Stage 1 fields (required) determine threat scope.
Stage 2 fields (optional) determine scenario specificity.

Boolean capability flags (``has_persistent_memory``, ``multi_agent``,
``hitl``) are computed properties derived solely from ``kc_subcodes``.
They cannot be set directly.  Legacy YAML profiles that include these
fields will have them silently stripped with a deprecation warning.

zones_active.description: Schneider zones active in the system. Minimum ['input', 'reasoning']. Other zones: 'tool_execution', 'memory', 'inter_agent'.
zones_active.title: Zones Active

entry_points.description: Attack entry points, each with a name, direction tag, and optional controllability. Direction is one of: input (attacker can send data in), output (system sends data out), bidirectional (both). Controllability is one of: direct (user types input), indirect (attacker influences data source), system (fully system-controlled), or null (inferred later).
entry_points.title: Entry Points

kc_subcodes.description: OWASP KC (Key Component) sub-codes identifying the system's granular capabilities. E.g. ['KC1.1', 'KC4.1', 'KC6.1.1']. Must contain at least one code.
kc_subcodes.title: Kc Subcodes

tool_inventory.description: Tools and APIs the system can invoke.  Required when 'tool_execution' is in zones_active.  Prevents phantom tool hallucination in downstream scenario generation.
tool_inventory.title: Tool Inventory

entry_point_completeness.description: Evidence/completeness state for the entry-point inventory. Inferred profiles are always 'inferred_partial'. Only operator-reviewed profiles may declare 'operator_confirmed_complete' with entry_point_evidence.

entry_point_evidence.description: Explicit evidence sources for operator_confirmed_complete entry-point inventory. Required when entry_point_completeness is operator_confirmed_complete.
entry_point_evidence.title: Entry Point Evidence

tool_inventory_completeness.description: Evidence/completeness state for the tool inventory. Inferred profiles are always 'inferred_partial'. Only operator-reviewed profiles may declare 'operator_confirmed_complete' with tool_inventory_evidence.

tool_inventory_evidence.description: Explicit evidence sources for operator_confirmed_complete tool inventory. Required when tool_inventory_completeness is operator_confirmed_complete.
tool_inventory_evidence.title: Tool Inventory Evidence

tool_types.description: Tools and APIs the system can invoke (populated at moderate/thorough depth).
tool_types.title: Tool Types

data_flows.title: Data Flows

EntryPoint.description:
An entry point with a direction tag indicating data flow.

Direction controls whether the entry point is considered as attacker
ingress during candidate expansion:
- ``input``: attacker can send data in (included in candidate cross-product)
- ``output``: system sends data out only (excluded from candidate cross-product)
- ``bidirectional``: both input and output (included in candidate cross-product)

Controllability (optional) indicates how directly an attacker can
influence data through this entry point:
- ``direct``: attacker types input directly (e.g. chat prompt)
- ``indirect``: attacker can influence a data source (e.g. RAG poisoning)
- ``system``: fully system-controlled, not attacker-accessible
- ``None``: inferred at runtime by keyword heuristic

The model is frozen (immutable) so that submitted metadata cannot be
mutated after the filter protocol has been engaged.

name.description: Entry point description, e.g. 'user prompts via chat widget'.
name.title: Name

entry_point_type.description: Typed ingress mechanism. This is adapter-neutral semantic metadata; it does not derive from the entry-point name.
entry_point_type.title: Entry Point Type

direction.description: Data flow direction: 'input' (attacker can send data in), 'output' (system sends data out), or 'bidirectional' (both).
direction.title: Direction

controllability.description: Attacker controllability: 'direct' (user types input), 'indirect' (attacker can influence data source), 'system' (fully system-controlled). When None, inferred by keyword heuristic.
controllability.title: Controllability

ingress_zone.description: Canonical Schneider zone for initial ingress through this entry point. When None, inferred from direction: input→input, bidirectional→input, output→output. This establishes canonical ingress-zone semantics in typed profile data rather than inferring from labels.
ingress_zone.title: Ingress Zone

EntryPoint.title: EntryPoint

ExternalIntegration.description:
An external system or service the agent integrates with.

The ``integration_id`` is a computed canonical identity (deterministic,
versioned, 128-bit) derived from the canonical name and integration type.
Application-assigned — the LLM never invents IDs.

name.description: Name of the external system (e.g. 'CRM', 'payment gateway')
name.title: Name

integration_type.description: How the agent connects to this system

data_sensitivity.description: Sensitivity of data accessible through this integration

supported_operations.description: Complete reviewed operation set; null means operation support is unknown
supported_operations.title: Supported Operations

ExternalIntegration.title: ExternalIntegration

IntegrationType.description: How the agent connects to an external system.
IntegrationType.title: IntegrationType

InventoryCompleteness.description:
Evidence/completeness state for entry-point and tool inventories.

``inferred_partial``: inference establishes presence, never absence.
``operator_confirmed_complete``: only an operator-reviewed profile may
declare this, with explicit evidence sources.  Ordinary LLM output
cannot self-promote.

ToolInventoryEntry.description:
A tool in the system's tool inventory (Stage 1).

Lightweight description of a tool or API the system can invoke,
extracted during Stage 1 capability profile inference.  Used to
ground downstream scenario generation — the LLM may only reference
tools listed here, preventing phantom tool hallucination.

The ``tool_id`` is a computed canonical identity (deterministic,
versioned, 128-bit) derived from the canonical tool name.
Application-assigned — the LLM never invents IDs.

supported_operations.description: Complete reviewed operation set; null means operation support is unknown
supported_operations.title: Supported Operations
